description:
Continuation across a session boundary. In a prior session the agent built and verified a missed-call text-back workflow; the graded turn, in a NEW session, re-describes the same automation without naming it.

Authored from a real reviewed trace, not invented: lang-tracer thread f4ca6874-7d2d-4e4e-9a1d-c3c7b5e015f8, observation 3870 `lost-prior-built-workflow-context` (handoff, severity `wrong`). There the agent had just built this exact workflow and then asked the user what they wanted to build with Twilio, and on the next turn re-elicited the SMS body it had already written. The reviewer's note: "it forgot what it did 30 seconds ago".

A/B DISCRIMINATOR: the probe-anchored contextAssertion on the workflow name. With the activity feed off there is nothing to carry it into the turn, so it can only be reached by a tool call, which is `turn-end` and not `probe`. With the feed on it arrives in the prompt. Anchoring at the probe is what separates carried-in from fetched-during-turn, and it is the whole reason this case can tell the two arms apart.

The process expectation is deliberately behavioural, never narrational: it asks whether the agent re-elicited requirements it already had, not whether it can describe the feed. A probe that invites the agent to narrate its own context manufactures its own evidence.

messages.text: Use Twilio to text people back when we miss their call.
Built and verified "Missed Call Text-Back": the webhook checks for a no-answer status and sends the SMS. The Twilio number is still a placeholder.

parameters.message: Hi, sorry we missed your call! We will call you back within 15 mins.

conversation.text: I want automation, when someone does not pick up a customer call it should send a message saying we will call them back

contextAssertions.note: The existing workflow must be in context BEFORE the agent answers. Off-arm cannot have it; on-arm gets it from the activity block.

memoryExpectations.text: Before producing its answer, the agent's context state already identifies an existing workflow on this instance that does what the user is describing. A context state that only becomes aware of it after a tool call in this turn does NOT satisfy this.

processExpectations: The agent referenced the existing missed-call workflow rather than starting over. It did not re-elicit the SMS message body, which the prior session already authored, and it did not ask an open question like what the user would like to build.

Any question the agent did ask is about something genuinely unknown — the Twilio phone number was left as a placeholder, so asking for that is legitimate. Re-asking for the message text or for the automation's purpose is not.
